title: Kiran v. State of U.P. and others
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner to apply under Clause 4.4 Annexure 4.2; licensee to consider in accordance with law after hearing stakeholders.
headnote: An occupier seeking a new connection after the recorded owner's death was not granted a connection on the writ. She was directed to apply as per Annexure 4.2 of Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 with an indemnity bond; the licensee was to consider that application in accordance with law after hearing persons having stake.
facts: The petitioner, Kiran, lived with her husband and children in House No. 290, Patel Nagar, Konch, District Jalaun, standing in the name of her father-in-law Rameshwar Prasad Soni, who died on 26 February 2024. She applied on 16 July 2024 for a new electricity connection in her own name and represented again on 23 July 2024. When no connection followed, she sought a mandamus for a new connection and for decision of that representation.

holding_units.topic: occupier new connection on indemnity application
holding_units.holding: The writ court will not itself grant a new connection to an occupier of premises standing in a deceased recorded owner's name. The applicant must move an application as per Annexure 4.2 of Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with the requisite indemnity bond; the licensee shall then consider it in accordance with law after hearing parties having stake.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner was entitled on merits to a new connection in her name
not_decided.note: The Court only directed a Clause 4.4 Annexure 4.2 application and consideration in accordance with law, without granting or refusing the connection.
